title: Canonical tensor comparison unit existence
statement: There exists an ordinary unit isomorphism satisfying the canonical normalization equation.

proof.text: Identify the underlying sheaf of I(R) with RI using moduleUnderlying at the rank-one module and ringUnderlying. Test moduleSMul on r times 1 equals r and use ringOne to show that the inverse underlying isomorphism sends r to r times the image of 1. This makes it a linear isomorphism from the unit RI-module to I(R), natural under restrictions. This construction also covers zero rings and empty sites.

Construct the scalar-extension unit isomorphism from the sectionwise linear equivalences S tensor_RI RI to S (AlgebraTensorModule.rid), and sheafify. The sheafification unit naturality and triangle identity show that its map sends the insertion of r to c(r). Compose this with scalar extension of the inverse of the preceding isomorphism, and transport along hobj to obtain j.

The sheafification monoidal functor laws and counit triangle identity show that the right unitor sends a pure tensor m tensor r to r times m. Express q as the scalar-extension unit transported along hobj; use hmap and naturality to make q natural. The scalar-extension adjunction shows that equality of module maps can be tested after q.

Precompose the desired equation with L of the inverse right unitor. Test it after q, using the preceding extensionality. Take the generalized test sheaf to be the underlying sheaf of M, with x the identity, y the constant section 1, and z the inverse right unitor. The pure equation for k, naturality of q and moduleUnderlying, and ringOne identify the resulting tensor with q(m) tensor an element sent to 1 by j. Apply tensor-map naturality and the right-unitor pure formula to obtain q(m). Cancel the invertible precomposition to conclude the original equation, with its statement unchanged.

      R)) ≅ SheafOfModules.unit ((sheafCompose JD (forget₂ CommRingCat.{u} RingCat.{u})).obj S) ,

        (k.mu M (SheafOfModules.unit ((sheafCompose JC (forget₂ CommRingCat.{u} RingCat.{u})).obj
      R))).hom ≫
